You are handed a report from the person who hit this. Reproduce it, find the cause, and fix the source. Do not change any test to agree with the code.

# chat: a reopened conversation draws none of the jobs it ran, and the job page becomes unreachable

## What happened

2026-09-03, base `dev@f38d6c01a`.

A conversation that ran background jobs yesterday draws **none of them** when it is
reopened. The column beside the transcript has no `jobs` section at all — not an empty
one, not a `0 jobs`, nothing — and because that section is the **only** door to a job's
page (there is no `/jobs` command and no key that opens one), the log of the work is no
longer reachable from the conversation that produced it. That is precisely the morning
when the log is the only thing left.

The engine keeps its half of the promise. `jobrow.go`'s own header states it as the law:

```
// What is reused is the RECORD-ROW SEAM an adaptive run's family opened
// ... and the checkpoint, so a conversation reopened tomorrow redraws what it
// ran rather than an empty column beside a transcript full of jobs.
```

and the replay site says the same thing again, in the comment directly above the send:

```
// A BACKGROUND JOB GOES OUT ON ITS OWN LANE, restored or not. ...
// A job replayed onto the task lane would reach a surface that correctly ignores
// it, and a conversation reopened tomorrow would draw none of the work it ran
// yesterday.
```

The surface is the half that is missing. The restored rows go out as
`session.EventJobUpdate` on the standing lane, and `internal/tui3`'s `taskEvent` — the
reducer for that lane — has **no case for that kind**, so every restored job falls off
the end of the switch and is dropped. The turn's own hub (`app.go`) does have the case,
which is why jobs are drawn perfectly while the window that started them is still open,
and why this has gone unseen: it is only ever wrong across a restart.

The manual already documents the behaviour that does not happen —
`internal/manual/chat/tasks.md` says *"Coming back, or reopening it, redraws the jobs it
ran, settled"* and *"the `jobs` section redraws the jobs this conversation started,
settled"*.

## Replication

**Deterministic (no model).** Everything here is in the repository; no key is needed
beyond a string the surface will accept, because nothing is ever sent.

1. `make build && make demo-home DEMO_HOME=/tmp/aforge-demo` — quit the surface it opens.
2. Pick any conversation folder in that home, e.g.
   `$(find /tmp/aforge-demo/.aforge/v3/projects -name transcript.jsonl -printf '%h\n' | head -1)`,
   and write a task checkpoint beside the transcript — this is exactly the shape
   `internal/session`'s `taskDocument`/`runRecord` writes for a background job that was
   still going when aforge closed:

   ```json
   {"type":"tasks","version":1,"seq":40,
    "nodes":[],
    "runs":[
     {"id":31,"title":"npm run dev","kind":"job","state":"failed","stopped":true,
      "report":"job 1 · log <that folder>/logs/jobs/1.log","elapsed_ms":2280000},
     {"id":32,"title":"make check","kind":"job","state":"done",
      "report":"job 2 · log <that folder>/logs/jobs/2.log","elapsed_ms":540000}
    ]}
   ```

   as `tasks.json` in that folder, and put any two files at those two log paths.
3. `cd /tmp/aforge-demo/aforge-v2 && HOME=/tmp/aforge-demo OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-demo <repo>/bin/aforge`,
   then press enter on the top card to open that conversation.

**What a developer sees today**, in the column: `standing` and its three rows, and then
nothing. No `jobs` line.

```
│ standing
│ ◦ the morning sweep
│ ? CI on master
│ ◦ the public API
│ + /standing
│
```

**What they should see** is the section, and the two rows under it when it is opened:

```
│ ▾ jobs · 2 ran
│   make check        2 · done
│   npm run dev    1 · stopped
```

**Field (real models, needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`).** In an ordinary conversation, ask for
something to be run in the background — a dev server, a long build — so the model calls
`bash` with `background:true` and the row appears in the `jobs` section. Quit with
`ctrl+c` twice. Reopen the same conversation (`aforge resume`, or picking it off home).
The section is gone. A few cents, under a minute.

## Where

`internal/tui3/task.go`, `app.taskEvent` — the switch on `ev.Kind` for the standing lane
(search `AN UPDATE IS ALSO WHAT MAKES THE "@" LIST STALE`). It has arms for
`EventTaskProposal`, `EventTaskUpdate`, `EventTaskPhase`, `EventStandingProposal`,
`EventTakeover` and `EventStandingUpdate`, and none for `EventJobUpdate`.

The engine side that sends them is `internal/session/task_run.go`,
`Agent.replayTaskRoster` (search `A BACKGROUND JOB GOES OUT ON ITS OWN LANE`). The
reducer that should receive them is `app.jobUpdate` in `internal/tui3/jobstate.go`, and
the section that draws them is `app.jobSection` in `internal/tui3/jobsection.go` — both
already exist and are already tested. Only the routing is missing.

## The fix

`app.taskEvent` grows the one arm the standing lane is missing, spelled the way the
turn's hub already spells it in `app.go`:

```go
case session.EventJobUpdate:
	if ev.Job != nil && a.jobUpdate(*ev.Job) {
		a.touch()
	}
```

The person-facing behaviour is the sentence the manual already carries: reopening a
conversation redraws the jobs it ran, settled — a job still going when aforge closed
comes back `stopped`, nothing is restarted, and its page opens on its log.

## Acceptance

- **e2e:** through the real binary, on the deterministic home above: after opening the
  restored conversation the column names `jobs · 2 ran`, and opening the section draws
  the rows `npm run dev` `1 · stopped` and `make check` `2 · done`. Today the string
  `jobs` does not appear in the column at all.
- **e2e:** the control — a conversation whose checkpoint has no job rows draws no `jobs`
  line, no label and no `0 jobs`, exactly as it does today (the emptiness law).
- **Unit:** `TestAReopenedConversationStillShowsItsJobs` in `internal/tui3` — three jobs
  handed to `app.taskEvent` as `session.EventJobUpdate` are kept by the window and named
  by `app.jobSection`; and `TestAJobReplayedOnTheStandingLaneOpensItsPage` — a job that
  arrived on the standing lane can be looked up by its number, so its page has a record
  to open.
- The manual page that covers this already quotes the wording
  (`internal/manual/chat/tasks.md`, "the column comes back after a restart") and needs no
  change: it was right and the surface was wrong. The change entry's `invalidates` names
  what people believed before.
